verdict.rationale: PostHog documents agent-driven flag management: its official MCP server can "create, update, schedule, and clean up flags," and agents can write across products. A CLI and an OpenAPI spec also exist. Nothing in the evidence shows approval workflows that force agent flag changes through review before reaching production. The "review proposed improvements and pull requests" line is about code changes, not flag-change approvals, so it earns no credit. missing for 10: documented approval/change-request workflow gating flag changes, evidence the CLI specifically manages flags, independent hands-on corroboration of agent flag toggling.

support.subject: As an AI agent, I can create and toggle flags through documented APIs, CLIs, or MCP — and the platform can force my changes through approval workflows instead of letting me write to production unreviewed

citations.quote: Create, update, schedule, and clean up flags from any MCP client or AI editor.
Once connected, your agent can read and write across PostHog's products.
Evaluate flags at runtime and manage flag definitions from your own tooling and CI.
